defects: (a) A RECORD LINE FIRST READ AGAINST THE WRONG CLOSING. The weight line's first draft quoted a closing hash other than b646's; caught before any write by grepping FINDINGS for the line opening "b646 closing" and re-drafted from it.
(b) ODD BACKTICKS IN A RECORD LINE. A possessive written with a backtick made the line's backtick count odd; the writer refused it, and the possessive was re-written with the typographic apostrophe.

(c) THE SORRY CENSUS`S BUILT MARK FOR TOML LAKEFILES. The first census read lean_lib roots from lakefile.lean alone and marked every TOML kernel's files TRACKED ONLY; repaired to read each lakefile's roots, its submodules and its import closure before the census was banked.
(d) REDIRECTED BANKS WRITTEN CR LF. Shell redirects wrote CR LF into banks at step zero; normalised to LF before the commit, every bank checked by byte count.
(e) A HELPER READER REFUSED AT THE CONCURRENCY LIMIT. The whole reading launched twenty-one helper readers against a limit of twenty; chunk 21 was refused and re-launched when a reader finished.

(f) HELPER READERS` CITE FORMS THE TABLE COULD NOT PARSE. Readers cited relay banks as relay:data/x:N, relay data/x:N, D:/relay/data/x:N and relay@data:x:N; the record tool's normaliser was widened twice (the last after the kernel banks' first run printed two unparsed cites) and two cites with no commit replaced by the seat with its reason.

(g) TWO HELPER READINGS EDITED AFTER HAND-BACK. The readers of chunks 10 and 12 changed their output files at 18:39 local, after the kernel banks' first commit (7ece93aa, 18:23); one change found a banked print the seat's control had missed. The banks were rewritten from the corrected readings and the change recorded in the joined bank; counts unchanged.

(h) THE CLASS-A CONTROL BLIND TO A PROFILE NAMED ACROSS KERNELS. The seat's control matched prints to the declarations of the row's own file, so SIDE-kernel Kernel/TriviumCode.lean:9, which names SIDE-cosmo's steane_parameters, escaped it; stated in the joined bank.

(i) A LINE-ENDING CHECK MISREAD AGAIN. bash's grep -c with $'\r' counted every line of the kernel banks as carrying a CR (b646's defect (d) repeated); Python's byte count read 0, and the banks were never CR LF.

(j) THE NAVIGATOR SCREEN`S FIRST PATTERN MISSING A LOCATION. The first screen over the rows' text caught a patent label and missed a drive path and "at D:"; widened before any bank was written, and the redactions written as patterns so the tool does not spell what they remove.

(k) A HEREDOC COLLAPSING A BACKSLASH IN A SCRATCH SCREEN. A python screen passed through a bash heredoc lost a backslash and raised on its own regex; re-written as a scratch file by the Write tool. No bank was touched.
(l) THE SAMPLE LITERAL TWO IDS SHORT. The navigator sample's literal omitted two drawn ids the seat had read; the table writer refused it as "not the sample drawn", and the two were added.

(m) THE SAMPLE`S AGREEMENT COUNTED BY EXACT MATCH. The navigator table's header counted "AGREE" by equality and printed 33 of 35 where two agreements carried a note; the count was made a prefix test before the bank was committed.

(n) THREE COMMANDS THE EDIT-ROUTE ARM READS AS OFFENCES. A stream edit by the seat on a scratch file in the scratchpad, a heredoc and a stream edit by two navigator helper readers on their scratch outputs; none touched tools/ or any repository, and the helper readers' brief did not forbid either form. G-EDIT-ROUTE fails on them and is declared failing on the face.

(o) A PLURAL POSSESSIVE IN A SEALED SHORT FORM. The record tool's short form of (f), "helper readers` cite forms", carries a backtick the ledger writer's apostrophe conversion does not reach (a space follows it), so the trail record's guard refused its odd count after the root, the tool sealed and no prompt allowed; and the short form of (h) carries a banned stem the ledger scanner refuses ("the class-A control" followed by the stem, read in memory as "unable to see a profile named across kernels"). The trail and this list were written by a scratch runner that imports the sealed tool unchanged, makes those two changes in memory and appends the short forms of (o) and (p), the sealed tool's bytes and hash untouched; the banks written before the root carry the sealed forms.

(p) DEFECT (n) AND THE LOCKED FACE MISNAME ONE OFFENCE. Re-read after the root, the edit-route arm's three offences are the seat's stream edit on a scratch file, one helper reader's stream edit on its scratch output, and one helper reader's `rm` of its scratch script by a relative name (not a heredoc, as (n) and section (0) of the locked face say); the face is not edited, the arm's reading stands as printed by the suite, and this line corrects the description.
